title: A ring map quasi-finite at a prime becomes finite on a factor after an etale extension with the same residue field (Algebra 00UJ)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings making $A$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra, let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, and assume that $\mathfrak q$ is an isolated point of the set $\{\mathfrak Q\in\operatorname{Spec}A:\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak p\}$ of primes of $A$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, with the subspace topology of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (that is, $R\to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$, Algebra, Definition 00PL, by Lemma 00PK (1) and the identification of this set with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$). Then there are a homomorphism of commutative rings $\psi:R\to R'$ which is etale (equivalently, $\operatorname{Spec}\psi:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]), a prime ideal $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ with $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak p$, an idempotent $e$ of $C=R'\otimes_RA$ (so that $C\cong C_e\times C_{1-e}$, with $C_e$ the localization at $\{1,e,e^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]) and a prime ideal $\mathfrak r\subset C$ such that: (1) the field map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ induced by $\psi$ is an isomorphism; (2) $C_e$ is a finite $R'$-module (via $R'\to C\to C_e$, $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$); (3) $\mathfrak r$ lies over $\mathfrak p'$ (its preimage under $R'\to C$ is $\mathfrak p'$), $e\notin\mathfrak r$, and $\mathfrak r$ is the only prime of $C$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$ and not containing $e$ (equivalently, $C_e$ has exactly one prime lying over $\mathfrak p'$); (4) the preimage of $\mathfrak r$ under $A\to C$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, is $\mathfrak q$. (Stacks Algebra 00UJ with $A=C_e$, $B=C_{1-e}$; its clause (5), that $B$ has no prime lying over both $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p'$, is not stated here.)
